title: Jump Game
description: You are given an integer array nums. You are initially positioned at the array's first index, and each element in the array represents your maximum jump length at that position. Return true if you can reach the last index, or false otherwise.
constraints: You must determine if the last index is reachable

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step from index 0 to 1, then 3 steps to the last index.
You will always arrive at index 3 with a jump length of 0, making it impossible to reach the last index.

title: Gas Station
description: There are n gas stations along a circular route, where the amount of gas at the ith station is gas[i]. You have a car with an unlimited gas tank and it costs cost[i] of gas to travel from the ith station to its next (i+1)th station. You begin the journey with an empty tank at one of the gas stations. Given two integer arrays gas and cost, return the starting gas station's index if you can travel around the circuit once in the clockwise direction, otherwise return -1. If there exists a solution, it is guaranteed to be unique.
constraints: If a solution exists, it is unique

examples.explanation: Starting at station 3, you can travel around the circuit once with fuel to spare.
There is no valid starting station that allows completing the circuit.

title: Task Scheduler
description: Given a characters array tasks, representing the tasks a CPU needs to do, where each letter represents a different task, and a non-negative integer n that represents the cooldown period between two same tasks, return the least number of units of time that the CPU will take to finish all the given tasks. In one unit of time, the CPU could complete either one task or just be idle.
constraints: tasks[i] is an uppercase English letter
Two identical tasks must be separated by at least n units of time

examples.explanation: One optimal schedule is A B idle A B idle A B, which takes 8 units of time.
With no cooldown, tasks can be executed back to back, taking 6 units of time.

title: Partition Labels
description: You are given a string s. We want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part. Return a list of integers representing the size of these parts.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
Each letter must appear in exactly one partition
The partitions must be contiguous substrings that together form s

examples.explanation: The partitions are 'ababcbaca', 'defegde', 'hijhklij', with lengths 9, 7, and 8.
The entire string must be one partition since letters overlap throughout.

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
description: There are some spherical balloons taped onto a flat wall that represents the XY-plane. The balloons are represented as a 2D integer array points where points[i] = [xstart, xend] denotes a balloon whose horizontal diameter stretches between xstart and xend. Arrows can be shot up directly vertically (in the positive y-direction) from different points along the x-axis. A balloon with xstart and xend is burst by an arrow shot at x if xstart <= x <= xend. Return the minimum number of arrows that must be shot to burst all balloons.
constraints: Balloons that only touch at endpoints can be burst by the same arrow

examples.explanation: One arrow can burst [1,6] and [2,8], and another can burst [10,16] and [7,12].
None of the balloons overlap, so each requires its own arrow.
